mcq.q: Which part of a computer is called its 'brain' because it executes every instruction and controls all other units?
mcq.e: The CPU executes instructions and controls the other units. Memory only stores and I/O devices only communicate.

mcq.q: The characteristic of a computer by which it can work for hours without creating any error and without tiring is called:
mcq.e: Diligence means working for long hours without error or complaint. Versatility means doing many kinds of work.

mcq.q: A computer is said to have 'no I.Q.' because it:
o: cannot think and only follows instructions
mcq.e: A computer has no intelligence of its own; it only follows the instructions given to it.

mcq.q: 1 picosecond is equal to:
mcq.e: pico = 10⁻¹². 10⁻⁹ is nano and 10⁻¹⁵ is femto.

mcq.q: 10⁻¹⁵ second is known as one:
mcq.e: femto = 10⁻¹⁵; atto is 10⁻¹⁸, pico is 10⁻¹².

mcq.q: Which of the following storage statements is FALSE?
mcq.e: 4 KB = 4 x 1024 = 4096 bytes, not 4069 (a digit-swap trap). The other statements are correct.

mcq.q: In the memory hierarchy, the cost per bit of storage is minimum in:
mcq.e: Cost per bit is highest in registers and lowest in magnetic tape.

mcq.q: Which generation of computers used transistors as the switching technology?
mcq.e: 1st = vacuum tubes, 2nd = transistors, 3rd = ICs, 4th = microprocessors (VLSI).

mcq.q: EDVAC stands for:
mcq.e: EDVAC = Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer, an early stored-program machine.

mcq.q: Which code is used by IBM mainframe computers, and in which unit is a supercomputer's speed measured?
mcq.e: Mainframes use IBM's 8-bit EBCDIC code, and supercomputer speed is measured in FLOPS (floating-point operations per second).

mcq.q: Which of the following number systems is NOT a positional number system?
mcq.e: The value of a Roman numeral digit does not depend on position, so Roman is non-positional.

mcq.q: What is the decimal value of the binary number 111111?
mcq.e: A number of n ones equals 2ⁿ − 1; with n = 6 this is 63.

mcq.q: What is (325) in decimal converted to octal?
mcq.e: 325 = 5 x 64 + 0 x 8 + 5, so it is 505 in octal.

mcq.q: (726) in octal equals which hexadecimal number?
mcq.e: 726 octal = 111 010 110 in binary; regrouped in 4 bits = 0001 1101 0110 = 1D6.

mcq.q: The binary number (1101010) equals which octal number?
mcq.e: Group in 3 bits from the right: 001 101 010 = 1, 5, 2.

mcq.q: What is the binary equivalent of the hexadecimal number (F4)?
The decimal number 213 written in base 4 is:
The sum (89D) in hexadecimal plus (259) in decimal equals what in decimal?
mcq.e: (89D)16 = 2048 + 144 + 13 = 2205; adding 259 gives 2464. Both must be brought to one base first.

mcq.q: What is (100001) in binary divided by (110) in binary, ignoring the remainder, written in binary?
mcq.e: 33 ÷ 6 = 5 (remainder ignored), and 5 = 101 in binary.

mcq.q: How many bits are needed to represent the numbers 0 to 2ⁿ − 1?
mcq.e: n bits give 2ⁿ distinct patterns covering 0 to 2ⁿ − 1.

mcq.q: What is the 2's complement of the binary number 101100?
mcq.e: Invert to 010011 (this is only the 1's complement), then add 1 to get 010100.

mcq.q: What is the 8-bit 2's complement representation of −8?
mcq.e: +8 = 00001000; invert to 11110111; add 1 to get 11111000. 11110111 is only the 1's complement.

mcq.q: What is the value of the 8-bit 2's complement number 10000000?
mcq.e: The MSB carries weight −2⁷, so 10000000 = −128, the value with no positive counterpart.

mcq.q: What is the minimum number of bits needed to represent −15 in 2's complement?
mcq.e: The 4-bit signed range is only −8 to +7, so 5 bits are needed: −15 = 10001.

mcq.q: Which 4-bit number is equal to its own 2's complement?
mcq.e: 1000 (−8) has no positive counterpart, so inverting and adding 1 gives 1000 again.

mcq.q: In IEEE-754 single precision, a 32-bit floating-point number is divided as:
mcq.e: IEEE-754 single precision uses 1 + 8 + 23 = 32 bits.

mcq.q: The decimal number 473 in BCD (8421) needs how many bits, compared with pure binary?
o: 12 bits in BCD; 9 bits in binary
9 bits in BCD; 12 bits in binary
mcq.e: BCD codes each of the 3 digits in 4 bits (0100 0111 0011 = 12 bits), while pure binary 473 needs only 9 bits.

mcq.q: The 8421 code 1000 corresponds to which Excess-3 code?
mcq.e: Excess-3 stores value + 3, so 8 + 3 = 11 = 1011.

mcq.q: How many XOR gates are needed to convert a 6-bit binary number to Gray code?
mcq.e: The MSB is copied and each other bit is XORed with its neighbour, so an n-bit number needs n − 1 XOR gates.

mcq.q: ASCII-7 can represent how many characters, and what is the ASCII value of 'A'?
mcq.e: ASCII is a 7-bit code with 2⁷ = 128 characters. A = 65 and a = 97.

mcq.q: Which code was created specifically because ASCII could not cover the world's languages?
mcq.e: Unicode, commonly encoded as variable-length ASCII-compatible UTF-8, covers world languages.

mcq.q: The assigned ordering among the characters used by a computer, which decides how text is sorted, is called:
mcq.e: The collating sequence is the character ordering. A cipher is a bit-level transformation ignoring linguistic structure.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the CPU's internal architecture?
mcq.e: The CPU has the ALU, control unit and registers. RAM is main memory outside the CPU, on the system bus.

mcq.q: Which register holds the address of the NEXT instruction to be executed?
mcq.e: The PC points to the next instruction; the IR holds the instruction currently being decoded.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a phase of the instruction cycle?
mcq.e: The cycle is Fetch, Decode, Execute, Store. 'Encode' is not a phase.

mcq.q: In a microprogrammed control unit, the control signals come from microinstructions that are stored in:
mcq.e: Microinstructions and microprograms are stored in control memory. Hardwired control uses fixed logic instead.

mcq.q: An array processor, with a single control unit broadcasting instructions to many processing elements, follows which model?
mcq.e: An array processor is SIMD; a multiprocessor is MIMD.

mcq.q: A third-generation microprocessor with a 24-bit address bus can address a maximum memory of:
mcq.e: 2²⁴ = 16 M locations, i.e. 16 MB.

mcq.q: Which statement about RISC is correct?
o: It uses few, simple, fixed-length instructions and is energy-efficient
Its instructions manipulate operands directly in memory
mcq.e: RISC has simple fixed-length instructions, hardwired control and register operands (ARM). The other options describe CISC.

mcq.q: Which addressing mode needs the largest number of memory references?
mcq.e: Indirect needs 2 references (pointer, then operand). Direct and register indirect need 1; immediate needs 0.

mcq.q: The instruction ADD R1, [R2] uses which addressing mode?
mcq.e: The brackets show that R2 holds the memory address of the operand: register indirect.

mcq.q: In a 7-stage pipeline, the 2nd instruction completes at the end of which clock cycle?
mcq.e: The n-th instruction completes at cycle k + (n − 1) = 7 + 1 = 8.

mcq.q: On a subroutine CALL, where is the return address saved?
mcq.e: The return address is pushed onto the stack; the stack pointer only marks the top of the stack.

mcq.q: Which memory stores each bit as charge on a capacitor and must be refreshed periodically?
mcq.e: DRAM uses capacitors whose charge leaks. SRAM uses flip-flops and needs no refresh.

mcq.q: EPROM is erased by:
o: Ultraviolet light, erasing the whole chip
mcq.e: EPROM is erased through its quartz window by UV light, and the whole chip erases (all bits become 1). EEPROM is byte-wise electrical.

mcq.q: How many address lines and data lines does a 2K × 16 memory need?
mcq.e: 2K = 2¹¹ words, so 11 address lines; data lines equal the word size, 16.

mcq.q: How many 16K × 1 memory chips are needed to build a 128K × 8 memory?
In a 4-way set-associative cache of 32 KB with 1 K block size and a 32 GB address space, how many TAG bits are there?
mcq.e: Address = 35 bits, offset = 10, lines = 32, sets = 32/4 = 8 so 3 set bits. TAG = 35 − 13 = 22.

mcq.q: A system has average access time 20 ns, cache 10 ns and main memory 110 ns. What is the cache hit ratio?
The storage-allocation scheme in which secondary memory can be addressed as though it were part of main memory is:
mcq.e: Virtual memory gives the illusion of an extremely large main memory (size illusion), whereas cache gives a speed illusion.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of data transfer between peripherals and memory?
mcq.e: Pipelining is a CPU technique, not an I/O transfer method.

mcq.q: In DMA, the mode in which one word at a time is moved between CPU cycles is called:
mcq.e: Cycle stealing moves one word at a time; burst transfer moves a whole block continuously.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid type of interrupt?
mcq.e: Valid types are hardware (external), software and internal (traps). There is no 'memory interrupt'.

mcq.q: Which device is used to read pencil marks on test and survey answer sheets?
mcq.e: OMR detects the presence or absence of marks. OCR reads printed characters; MICR reads magnetic ink on cheques.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an impact printer?
mcq.e: A dot-matrix printer strikes an inked ribbon with pins. Ink-jet, laser and thermal are non-impact.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a direct-access storage device?
mcq.e: Magnetic tape supports only sequential access.

mcq.q: In MS-Word, which shortcut key justifies the selected paragraph?
mcq.e: Ctrl+J = justify, Ctrl+T = hanging indent, Ctrl+H = find and replace, Ctrl+Y = redo.

tf.s: The Control Unit performs the actual processing on data and so replaces the ALU.
tf.n: The control unit coordinates the whole system but performs no actual processing on data; the ALU does the calculations.

tf.s: A 4-bit signed 2's complement number can range from −8 to +7.
tf.n: The range is −2ⁿ⁻¹ to +2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1; for n = 4 this is −8 to +7.

tf.s: The largest 4-digit number in base 7 is 7777.
tf.n: Base-7 digits run only from 0 to 6, so the largest 4-digit number is 6666.

tf.s: The XOR operation outputs 1 only when its two inputs differ.
tf.n: XOR acts as a difference detector.

tf.s: A Las Vegas style fixed-time claim: the Excess-3 code is a self-complementing code.
tf.n: Excess-3 stores digit + 3 and is a self-complementing code.

tf.s: Static memory (SRAM) must be refreshed periodically, like DRAM.
tf.n: SRAM uses flip-flops and needs no refresh; DRAM uses capacitors and must be refreshed.

tf.s: Memory cycle time equals access time plus recovery time.
tf.n: It is the minimum delay between two successive memory operations.

tf.s: Only one bit in an instruction is needed to distinguish direct from indirect addressing.
tf.n: A single mode bit selects between direct and indirect.

tf.s: A k-stage pipeline needs k cycles to fill before the first instruction completes and the 5-stage case takes 5 extra cycles.
tf.n: A k-stage pipeline needs k − 1 cycles to fill; a 5-stage pipeline needs 4, after which one instruction completes per cycle.
The ALU does arithmetic, logic, comparison and shifts; memory addressing is on the control unit side.

tf.s: ROM is volatile memory that loses its content when power is switched off.
tf.n: ROM is non-volatile and read-only; RAM is the volatile memory.

tf.s: Programmed I/O requires constant monitoring of the device status by the CPU.
tf.n: The CPU polls the status flag in a loop, unlike interrupt-driven I/O and DMA.

tf.s: ASCII is an 8-bit code with 256 characters.
tf.n: ASCII is a 7-bit code with 128 characters; Extended ASCII and EBCDIC are 8-bit.

tf.s: COM (Computer Output Microfilm) can be used for data entry.
tf.n: COM is an output method only, so it cannot do data entry.
